answer_text:
Let

\[
B_L=\left\{(x,y):\sqrt{(x-7)^2+(y+3)^2}<L\right\}.
\]

We want the largest \(L\) such that \(G\) is invertible on \(B_L\).

The map is

\[
G(x,y)=\bigl((x-1)^2,y^4\bigr).
\]

If two points have the same image, then

\[
(x-1)^2=(x'-1)^2 \quad\text{and}\quad y^4=(y')^4.
\]

Thus

\[
x'=x \quad\text{or}\quad x'=2-x,
\]
and

\[
y'=y \quad\text{or}\quad y'=-y.
\]

So \(G\) identifies points reflected across the line \(x=1\) and the line \(y=0\). Near \(t=(7,-3)\), we are in the region

\[
x>1,\qquad y<0.
\]

In that region, the map is one-to-one because:

- \((x-1)^2\) is one-to-one for \(x>1\),
- \(y^4\) is one-to-one for \(y<0\).

The ball centered at \((7,-3)\) stays inside the region \(x>1,y<0\) as long as it does not touch either line \(x=1\) or \(y=0\).

The distances from \(t=(7,-3)\) to these lines are

\[
d(t,\{x=1\})=|7-1|=6,
\]

\[
d(t,\{y=0\})=|-3-0|=3.
\]

The closer obstruction is \(y=0\), so the largest possible radius is \(3\).

For \(L=3\), we have

\[
|x-7|<3,\qquad |y+3|<3,
\]

so

\[
4<x<10,\qquad -6<y<0.
\]

Thus \(x>1\) and \(y<0\) throughout the neighborhood, and \(G\) is invertible there, with inverse

\[
G^{-1}(u,v)=\left(1+\sqrt{u},-v^{1/4}\right)
\]

on the image.

If \(L>3\), choose \(0<\varepsilon<\min(3,L-3)\). Then both points

\[
p=(7,\varepsilon),\qquad q=(7,-\varepsilon)
\]

lie in \(B_L\), but

\[
G(p)=\bigl(36,\varepsilon^4\bigr)=G(q),
\]

while \(p\neq q\). Hence \(G\) is not invertible on \(B_L\).

Therefore the largest such \(L\) is

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
